docs.h:
Welcome to EQM

EQM is a world of war in the frozen north, the deep woods and the burning sands. Here you do not play the folk of Qeynos or Freeport: you are one of the peoples they feared. Giants, golems and orcs, goblins, rat-folk and brownies, sarnak, lizardmen and kobolds. Each people keeps a city, each city keeps an alliance, and anyone within reach of your level may be your enemy, your own kin among them.

The peoples

Making a character takes two pages. On the first you choose your people and a kind of it; on the second your name, your class (only the callings your people know are offered) and your stats. The kind is only your look: every kind of a people fights the same.

The Spirit orc and the Spirit goblin are pale and see-through, and like the Sarnak spirit and the Sarnak skeleton they count as undead.

Callings

Each people follows the callings it has always known:

PeopleClasses

OrcWarrior, Rogue, Shaman

RodentWarrior, Cleric, Paladin, Ranger, Druid, Rogue, Shaman, Necromancer

LizardmanWarrior, Cleric, Shadow Knight, Monk, Shaman, Necromancer
KoboldWarrior, Cleric, Paladin, Ranger, Druid, Monk, Bard, Rogue, Shaman

The three alliances

  • The Frostfell alliance: giants, golems and orcs.
  • The Greenwood alliance: goblins, rodents and brownies.
  • The Dunelands alliance: sarnak, lizardmen and kobolds.

Every city keeps its own standing with you. Your own city starts out Kindly toward you, your allies' cities Amiable, and the other alliances' cities Dubious. A Dubious city's merchants will not trade with you, but its guards leave you be unless you sink to Scowls. Kill a city's people and it, and its allies, will think less of you.

Alliances are a matter of standing only. They do not keep you safe from other players.

Your first steps

  1. Your Guild Note. You arrive carrying a Guild Note. Hand it to your class's guildmaster in your home city: you earn your first training tunic, a little experience, and the name of the master who will teach you your epic once you reach level 46.
  2. Around the city (levels 1 to 6): the beasts of your home land, close to the walls.
  3. The road out (levels 6 to 15): the road from your city to the edge of your home land grows more dangerous the farther you walk.
  4. The wide lands (levels 15 to 35): Everfrost Peaks, Dagnor's Cauldron and the Field of Bone, each joined to one home land and to each other.
  5. The deep places (levels 25 to 55): the dungeons, the dragons' lairs, the planes of the gods and the great temples.

A few of the old cities' errands are still asked: Mazziana Ridgerunner in Kelethin pays for orc scalps (ask her about the [orcs]), Bjoskhua Blackfist waits in Kael Drakkel, and Hasten Bootstrutter on the north shore of Dagnor's Cauldron makes Journeyman's Boots for those who bring him what he needs.

The lands

Many of the old lands are only part of what they once were: the roads beyond their edges are closed.

Fighting other players

  • Anyone within five levels of you is fair game, your own alliance included. A level 25 fights levels 20 to 30, and no one else can touch them, nor they anyone else.
  • The highest level is 50.
  • A group holds at most four. The greatest foes of the world are made for two groups fighting side by side.
  • Guards take sides. When players fight beside a city's guards, the guards help the one their city likes better.
  • Out-of-character talk (/ooc) carries to every land.

Death and loot

  • Slain by a player, you lose no experience. Slain by a monster, you lose it as always.
  • The whole world hears of it: every player learns who slew whom.
  • The winner may take your coin and one item from your corpse, worn, carried or in a bag, the winner's choice. No-drop items can never be taken. The treasures of the planes, the gods and the great dragons are no-drop.
  • You wake at your bind point. At first that is your home city. Casters who know the art can bind where the old world allowed it.

The class epics

At level 46 every class may earn its epic: the weapon or charm its masters have carried since the old days. Each class has one epic master, a guildmaster in one city (the Beastlord has two). Hail them and ask about the [epic]. Every epic follows the same road:

  1. The master tells the tale. Say you are [ready], and the master writes a sealed letter to the city's smith.
  2. Give the letter to the smith (the weaponsmith; the monks' armorer). The smith reads it and names the first two pieces: ask about each by its name in [brackets] to hear where it is and why the work needs it.
  3. The first piece is carried by a rare beast of the wide lands.
  4. The second is held by a named foe of a dungeon.
  5. Bring both to the smith, who makes the half-made work and sends you back to your master.
  6. Show the half-made work to the master (give it; you get it back). Only then does the master explain the last two pieces: ask about each by its name.
  7. The third piece lies in the planes or in Tunare's grove.
  8. The fourth is taken from one of the great foes, a fight for two groups.
  9. Bring the half-made work and the last two pieces to the master: the epic is yours.

The pieces, the letter and the half-made work are no-drop: no one can trade them to you, and no one can take them from your corpse. A rare beast does not always carry its piece; a great foe gives up one of its pieces, sometimes two, every time it falls. Lost the letter? Tell your master you are [ready] again. Hail the master or the smith to hear where you stand.

Journeyman's Boots: Hasten Bootstrutter still asks what he always asked. Bring him a Shadowed Rapier, a Ring of the Ancients and 3250 gold (or the same in platinum), and he will make you the boots.

Treasures that stayed where they were

  • The primal velium weapons (battle axe, battlehammer, brawl stick, claidhmore, reinforced bow, spear, war lance and warsword): the four Warders of Sleeper's Tomb.
  • Trakanon's hoard: Trakanon, in Old Sebilis.
  • The dragons' hoards: the dragons of Veeshan's Peak and of the Temple of Veeshan keep their own.
  • The gods' and kings' treasures: Tunare in her grove in Greenwood; King Tormax, the Statue of Rallos Zek and the Avatar of War in Kael Drakkel; Dain Frostreaver IV in the snowfield of Frostfell.
  • Efreeti Lord Djarn's treasure: the Efreeti Lord, a rare guest of Nagafen's Lair.

The Velious armour

The armourers of the north still forge their old armour for those their people trust. You need Kindly standing or better with their city. A city's own people start there; its allies must earn it.

  • Kael Drakkel's armourers stand in Kael Drakkel's hall, one for each calling and kind of armour.
  • Skyshrine's armourers (the Fe'Dhar and Far'Huin smiths) stand around Skyshrine's upper hall.
  • The Coldain smiths, lorekeepers and Royal Armorer Slade keep a camp in Frostfell's snowfield, beside Dain Frostreaver himself. They answer to the camp's own standing: the Frostfell alliance starts there Kindly, everyone else Dubious.

The ancient tarnished pieces, gems and parts they ask for drop in EQM's own lands: most in the Temple of Veeshan and in Velketor's Labyrinth, and the rest from the Temple of Veeshan's common dragonkind.

Spells

The highest level is 50, so the world keeps nothing beyond it: no item that needs a level above 50 drops, is sold or can be made, and no scroll above level 50 drops or is sold. Every spell up to 50 is sold by the scribes of the cities.

Your first gear

Every new adventurer carries a Guild Note. Give it to your class's guildmaster in your home city for your class's training tunic and a word about your epic.

The cities

Nine cities stand in the three home lands, three to an alliance. They all offer the same services, so no one must travel far for training or gear. Only their epic masters and the foes nearby differ.

What every city offers

  • A banker to keep your coin and goods.
  • The Merchant for general goods, with the reagents your spells use up (bone chips, gems, fish scales, bat wings and the bard's instruments among them).
  • The Grocer for food and drink, the Weaponsmith for weapons and the Armorer for armour and shields.
  • Scribes selling every spell up to level 50 for every class that casts: Cleric, Paladin, Ranger, Shadow Knight, Druid, Bard, Shaman, Necromancer, Wizard, Magician and Enchanter (and, in Kael Drakkel and Skyshrine, the Beastlord). A class with many spells has two or three scribes, each sorted by level ("Wizard spells 1-28", "Wizard spells 28-49").
  • A guildmaster of every class, who trains you and takes your Guild Note. Kael Drakkel and Skyshrine also keep a Beastlord guildmaster and a Beastlord scribe, for the giants and golems who bond with a warder.
  • Guards in the streets and at the city's mouth. They defend the city's friends and, in a fight between players, the one the city likes better.

A city's merchants will not trade with you once its standing toward you falls to Dubious or worse. Your own alliance's cities welcome you; the other alliances' cities will not trade with you at first.

The bosses

Every city has great foes close by, and the deep places hold the greatest of all. Bosses come in two kinds:

  • Named foes, for one group of four. They return about 45 minutes after they fall.
  • Great foes, for two groups of four fighting side by side. They return in four to eight hours, not in days.

Levels are the foe's own; bring a group of your level or near it.

Sleeper's Tomb (a gate on the central plateau of Everfrost Peaks)

  • The four Warders (54): Hraashna, Nanzata, Tukaarak and Ventani. They guard the primal velium weapons.
